name: Rudy Yakym III
signature: Northern Indiana Republican who cheers Amazon's $15 billion data center build in his district, wants federal permitting out of the way, frames AI as a race with China, and is backed by the Leading the Future AI super PAC.

notable_quote.text: We need to maintain this. We're in a race against China for leadership in this space. Someone is going to win, and it should be us.

data_centers.summary: Yakym celebrates the Amazon data center campuses in his district as jobs and tax base, cosponsors a bill to speed new power plants onto the grid, and says the fix for AI's energy appetite is more energy production and less federal permitting review. No statements found raising ratepayer, water, or community concerns.

evidence.title: Quoted in WNDU on Amazon's $15 billion northern Indiana data center announcement
evidence.quote: As our country races to lead in artificial intelligence and advanced computing, investments like this ensure we are building that future here at home and delivering new opportunities for hardworking Hoosier families.
evidence.what_it_shows: He welcomed the Amazon data center expansion in his district as good-paying jobs and a bigger tax base, with no conditions attached.

evidence.title: Washington Reporter interview: eight GOP lawmakers on an AI deal with KOSA and how to lower energy costs
evidence.quote: I just got a bill passed that reforms NEPA, which has gone way too far. Previously, we were prevented from building pipelines and transmission lines.
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked how to lower energy costs as AI demand grows, he called for more energy exploration and getting the federal government out of the way of pipelines and transmission lines.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 1047, the GRID Power Act (joined May 15, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: The bill tells federal regulators to speed dispatchable power plants through the interconnection queue, a supply-side answer to load growth from data centers.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Yakym Votes for Government Efficiency and Energy Dominance (SPEED Act)
evidence.quote: For years, NEPA has imposed unnecessary red tape that delays critical infrastructure projects, slows economic growth, and limits domestic energy production
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs permitting reform so energy and infrastructure projects get built faster.

ai_risk.summary: Asked about AI rules, Yakym put winning the AI race with China first and limited the guardrails he wants to kids' online safety and AI-enabled crime. He also pressed Medicare to use predictive AI tools more, and the industry-backed Leading the Future super PAC and Anthropic's PAC both support him.

evidence.title: Washington Reporter interview: asked whether he would back an AI bill preempting states if it included KOSA-style kids protections
evidence.quote: Someone is going to win, and it should be us. We've also got to ensure we protect our kids as they go online and make sure that there are some guardrails so you can't have people committing crimes with AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats AI mainly as a race the United States must win, with guardrails narrowed to children and crime rather than broad safety rules.

evidence.title: Leading the Future super PAC names Yakym a 'House GOP Champion'
evidence.quote: these House members will be critical to advancing a national framework in Congress that sets basic safety standards, protects children and families, and ensures America leads with confidence
evidence.what_it_shows: The AI industry's main super PAC, which backs a light national framework, lists him among 12 House Republicans it supports as having engaged with the industry.

evidence.title: FEC filing: AnthroPAC (Anthropic's PAC) gave $1,000 to Rudy for Indiana
evidence.what_it_shows: Anthropic's corporate PAC contributed $1,000 to his campaign committee on June 29, 2026.

evidence.title: Press release: Yakym Calls Out $60 Billion of Fraud (Ways and Means hearing)
evidence.quote: pushed for answers on whether federal law or regulation prevents CMS from deploying the same real-time claims analytics and predictive AI tools that Medicare Advantage plans and private insurers routinely use
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants government to adopt AI tools faster and framed existing rules as a possible obstacle, not a safeguard.

tech_regulation.summary: Yakym cosponsored the House Kids Online Safety Act in 2024 and says any AI deal must protect kids online. No positions found on Section 230, antitrust, or broad privacy law.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 7891, Kids Online Safety Act (118th Congress), joined Sept 17, 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: He signed on to the main kids' online safety bill, which requires apps to protect minors from harmful content and addictive design.

evidence.title: Washington Reporter interview on an AI deal with KOSA
evidence.quote: We've also got to ensure we protect our kids as they go online and make sure that there are some guardrails so you can't have people committing crimes with AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: He ties kids' online protections to any federal AI package.

preemption.summary: Asked point-blank in January 2026 whether he would support preempting state AI laws in exchange for KOSA-style kids protections, Yakym did not object and stressed winning the AI race, which the interviewer read as openness to the deal. He also voted for H.R. 1 when it carried the 10-year state AI-law moratorium and is backed by a super PAC pushing a national framework, but he has not stated a clear position in his own words.

evidence.title: Washington Reporter interview: eight GOP lawmakers on an AI deal with KOSA
evidence.quote: Both Yakym and Harrigan sounded willing to consider a potential legislative compromise that would include federal preemption of state-based AI regulations as well as protections for children like what had been in versions of the KOSA.
evidence.what_it_shows: This is the reporter's characterization; his own answer to the preemption question was about staying ahead of China and protecting kids, without endorsing or rejecting preemption.

evidence.title: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), which then included a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: The House-passed budget bill carried the state AI-law moratorium; a Yea on the whole package is weak evidence on preemption by itself.

evidence.title: Leading the Future super PAC 'House GOP Champions' list
evidence.what_it_shows: The PAC backing him says these members will be critical to passing a national AI framework in Congress, the industry's preferred alternative to state laws.

china_chips.summary: Looked for statements on Nvidia sales, chip export controls, or the GAIN AI, Chip Security, and AI OVERWATCH bills and found none. His China comments are about trade overcapacity and tariffs, not AI chips.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Yakym Urges Coordination to Hold China Accountable (Ways and Means hearing with USTR)
evidence.quote: China's promise to shift to a consumption economy remains just that, a promise
evidence.what_it_shows: He is hawkish on Chinese trade practices but has not taken a position on AI chip exports.

search_notes: Searched Google News for Yakym with: artificial intelligence; data center; chatbot/deepfake/KOSA; Nvidia/export controls; Leading the Future/AnthroPAC; Amazon New Carlisle; energy costs/GRID Power Act; TikTok/Section 230/Big Tech; One Big Beautiful Bill AI moratorium; Washington Reporter; Fulton County data center. Paginated all 14 pages of his press releases at yakym.house.gov/media-center/press-releases (site keyword filter does not work) and read the SPEED Act, Times Union year-in-review, HHS hearing, fraud hearing, and China trade releases. Read the Washington Reporter Jan 20, 2026 interview in full (his transcript includes the direct preemption/KOSA question). Verified the Leading the Future endorsement at Breitbart and the AnthroPAC $1,000 contribution through the FEC API. Verified GRID Power Act cosponsorship in the govinfo BILLSTATUS XML and the H.R. 1 Yea vote on govtrack. Google News link decoding was rate-limited for most of the session, so some hits (Legis1, South Bend Tribune opinion, WSBT Fulton County) could not be opened. Did not find him on any AI caucus roster; committee assignment is Ways and Means.

name: Marlin A. Stutzman
signature: Financial Services member who sits on the digital assets, fintech and AI subcommittee; his FUTURES Act to modernize bank regulators' technology passed committee 52-0, but he has said almost nothing publicly about AI policy or data centers.

notable_quote.text: The modernization of the regulatory technology our American financial systems rely on is essential. The FUTURES Act will help Congress better understand the red tape keeping our regulators in the past while our financial institutions race into the future.

data_centers.summary: No public statements found on data centers as of Sept 2026, even though Google and Amazon projects around Fort Wayne sit in his district. Searched his press releases, Google News, and local Fort Wayne coverage for data centers, electric rates, and Indiana Michigan Power.

ai_risk.summary: No stance found on AI safety rules. The closest item is his FUTURES Act, which orders bank regulators to assess and upgrade their technology; his Democratic co-lead framed it around AI-driven bank-run risk, but Stutzman's own words did not mention AI.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Stutzman and Rep. Foster introduce the FUTURES Act
evidence.quote: New threats to our financial institutions arise daily, and Congress must be proactive in our approach to stopping them.
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill has regulators report on modernizing their supervision technology; only co-lead Bill Foster tied it to AI accelerating bank runs.

evidence.title: Press release: Stutzman's bipartisan FUTURES Act passes House Financial Services Committee 52-0
evidence.quote: The FUTURES Act will help Congress better understand the red tape keeping our regulators in the past while our financial institutions race into the future.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames the issue as regulators lagging technologically behind the firms they oversee, not as a case for new AI rules.

tech_regulation.summary: His only tech-rules action found is cosponsoring a small bill giving car owners control over the data their connected cars collect. No positions found on Section 230, antitrust, kids online safety, or broader privacy law.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 6734, Auto Data Privacy and Autonomy Act (joined Sept 2, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: A narrow data-privacy bill for connected cars; a single minor cosponsorship, so confidence is low.

preemption.summary: No statement found on preempting or pausing state AI laws. He voted for H.R. 1 when it carried the 10-year moratorium, but his statement on that vote talked only about taxes, Medicaid, the border and the budget, so the vote alone is not treated as a position.

evidence.title: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), which then included a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: The House-passed budget bill carried the state AI-law moratorium; a Yea on the whole package is weak evidence on preemption by itself.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Stutzman votes to pass the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
evidence.quote: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act is the start of America's return to fiscal sanity
evidence.what_it_shows: His explanation of the vote never mentions the AI moratorium, so it cannot be read as a preemption stance.

china_chips.summary: Searched for Nvidia, chip export controls, TikTok, and China technology statements and found nothing; his China-related activity is on foreign policy and trade, not AI chips.

search_notes: Searched Google News for Stutzman with: artificial intelligence; data center Indiana; fintech/Financial Services AI hearing; deepfake/chatbot/Section 230/Big Tech; electricity/utility bills/Indiana Michigan Power/ratepayers; China chips/TikTok/export controls/Nvidia; Leading the Future/Public First; Google/Amazon Fort Wayne data center; nuclear/energy demand/grid reliability; the AI subcommittee by name; primary opponent Kenworthy and Journal Gazette coverage. Read all 5 pages of press releases at stutzman.house.gov (Jan 2025 to Jul 2026), the committees and caucuses page (member of the Financial Services Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence; no AI caucus), the In the News page (empty), and both FUTURES Act releases plus the OBBB vote release. Checked the Dec 10, 2025 HFSC AI hearing page on C-SPAN for his remarks (none listed). Verified the H.R. 1 Yea vote on govtrack. No AI super PAC support or attacks found. Google News link decoding was rate-limited, so the South Bend Tribune opinion piece and a CBA fraud-legislation statement could not be opened.

name: James R. Baird
signature: Science and Foreign Affairs member who wrote a voluntary NIST AI-guidelines bill and an export-control reform bill, cosponsors the AI OVERWATCH Act to block advanced chip sales to China, and says local zoning should decide data center siting.

notable_quote.text: The bills we passed today are critical to addressing the security challenges with AI, providing Congress with oversight over the sale of advanced AI chips to our adversaries, and supercharging American AI leadership to beat China.

data_centers.summary: Baird says data centers have value and will raise energy needs, and he trusts local planning and zoning to sort out where they go rather than Washington. His answer to rising power demand is more baseload generation like coal, not limits on new load. No statements found on who pays for grid upgrades.

evidence.title: E&E News: Data center boom creates political conundrum for the GOP (Baird quoted)
evidence.quote: We know the value of data centers. We know it's going to increase the energy needs, and so I have great faith in our local people to take care of that.
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports data centers, acknowledges the power demand, and wants local officials rather than the federal government to manage the tradeoffs; the article notes a local group in his district organizing against two proposed facilities.

evidence.title: E&E News: Baird on local authority over data center siting
evidence.quote: This is why we have these planning and zoning processes. The local people have a chance to put in their say.
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs local governments' power to approve or reject data centers that do not fit community needs.

evidence.title: Press release: Congressman Baird joins President Trump for White House clean coal executive order event
evidence.quote: As energy demand continues to grow, we need dependable energy sources like coal to protect our grid reliability.
evidence.what_it_shows: His response to growing electricity demand is keeping coal plants running for reliability, not slowing new load.

ai_risk.summary: Mixed. Baird wrote a bill for voluntary, non-binding NIST guidelines on AI development and stressed it gives NIST no regulatory power, and he frames AI as a race to beat China. But he also cosponsors the DEFIANCE Act, a binding rule letting victims sue over AI sexual deepfakes, and backs age verification and child-safety bills.

evidence.title: House Science Committee markup remarks on his AI Development Practices Act (transcript via Tech Policy Press)
evidence.quote: If we hope to do further research and development in the AI technology then I think we also need appropriate guidelines for its development. So that's why I introduced the AI Development Practices Act.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants guidelines for AI developers, but through NIST studying industry practice rather than mandates.

evidence.title: House Science Committee markup: Baird stresses his bill is voluntary and non-regulatory
evidence.quote: It simply tasks them with studying the standards of AI development and any guidelines they publish will be entirely voluntary with no force of law behind them
evidence.what_it_shows: He deliberately kept the bill from giving NIST any regulatory power, the light-touch approach.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 9466, AI Development Practices Act of 2024 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Has NIST catalog voluntary practices for communicating an AI system's transparency, robustness, security, and safety characteristics; passed committee by voice vote.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 3562, DEFIANCE Act of 2025 (joined Aug 27, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: Lets people sue anyone who makes or shares AI-generated sexual images of them without consent, a binding rule for a specific AI harm.

evidence.title: Press release: Baird applauds House Foreign Affairs Committee passage of AI security bills including the AI OVERWATCH Act
evidence.quote: providing Congress with oversight over the sale of advanced AI chips to our adversaries, and supercharging American AI leadership to beat China
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI policy as national security and beating China rather than as model-safety regulation.

tech_regulation.summary: Baird supports targeted rules aimed at kids and foreign-controlled apps: he voted to force TikTok's Chinese owner to sell, cosponsored the ACES Act against Chinese-controlled social media, and cosponsors the SCREEN Act age-verification bill and the STOP CSAM Act. No positions found on Section 230 repeal, antitrust, or comprehensive privacy law.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Baird votes to protect Americans from the influence of Communist China (H.R. 7521 TikTok divestiture)
evidence.quote: Communist China cannot have free rein to push its agenda on the American people and manipulate our children
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed forcing TikTok's parent to divest, framing it as protecting children and public discourse from a foreign adversary.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 1623, SCREEN Act (joined Aug 26, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires adult websites to verify users' ages so kids cannot get in.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 3921, STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (joined June 15, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: Makes platforms do more to report and remove child sexual abuse material and lets victims sue them for failing.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 4927, ACES Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Cracks down on TikTok and other Chinese-controlled social media apps over spying concerns.

preemption.summary: No statement found on preempting or pausing state AI laws. He voted for H.R. 1 when it carried the 10-year moratorium, but that vote alone is not treated as a position, and his local-control comments to E&E News were about data center zoning, not AI rules.

evidence.title: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), which then included a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: The House-passed budget bill carried the state AI-law moratorium; a Yea on the whole package is weak evidence on preemption by itself.

china_chips.summary: Baird wants tighter export controls on advanced technology to China. He sponsored a bill letting the State, Defense, and Energy departments propose export-control rules and requiring review of China's military-civil fusion strategy, cosponsors the AI OVERWATCH Act giving Congress power to block advanced AI chip sales to China, and says chips must not give China the upper hand.

evidence.title: Sponsor of H.R. 8036, Interagency Coordination in Export Controls Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Ends Commerce's monopoly on writing export-control rules, requires three of four departments to agree, and orders review of China's military-civil fusion; passed the Foreign Affairs Committee in April 2026.

evidence.title: Press release: Baird's Interagency Coordination in Export Controls Act passes House Foreign Affairs Committee
evidence.quote: China is notorious for importing and stealing American and allied civilian technologies and maliciously using them in support of its military. We cannot allow our advanced technologies to give China the upper hand.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words, the goal of his export-control bill is keeping advanced American technology away from China's military.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 6875, AI OVERWATCH Act (joined Jan 16, 2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: Gives Congress the power to block sales of advanced AI chips to China and other risky countries before they happen.

evidence.title: Press release: Baird applauds passage of legislation to improve AI security in House Foreign Affairs Committee
evidence.quote: The bills we passed today are critical to addressing the security challenges with AI, providing Congress with oversight over the sale of advanced AI chips to our adversaries, and supercharging American AI leadership to beat China.
evidence.what_it_shows: He celebrated committee passage of the AI OVERWATCH Act, which he cosponsors, as curbing chip sales to China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 6603, No Technology for Terror Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Tightens rules so American chips and components cannot reach Iran's drone and weapons programs.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of H.R. 802, STAR Act of 2025 (joined Feb 10, 2025)
evidence.what_it_shows: Extends the tax credit for building chip factories in America; supports domestic chipmaking rather than an export position.
